sn1.2:1.1: From here, the Pali gives only the abbreviated setting or none at all. In such cases, we are meant to read the full introduction per [sn1.1]().
sn1.2:5.1: The Buddha’s answer seems to mix a few lines of verse with some prose. The Chinese parallels at SA 1268 and SA-2 179 treat the whole of the Buddha’s answer as prose, the verse being spoken by the deity at the end. This line does, however, seem to be verse, as it has an unusual structure, best understood as due to the exigencies of metre, where it occurs elsewhere it is always as verse. Perhaps only this line and the next should be understood as verse, as the remainder is not metrical.
sn1.2:5.2: With this the Buddha differentiates himself from Yājnavalkya, for whom perception (limited awareness) ends, but consciousness (infinite awareness) is eternal (Bṛhadāraṇyaka Upaniṣad 2.4.12).
